digest.component_or_area: plan-review Pass-2 prerequisite verifier and LLM-Review gate (Bedrock/Anthropic structured output routing)
propositions: Plan-review Pass-2 prerequisite_verify and code-review LLM-Review gate fail with HTTP 400 ValidationException when Bedrock cannot compile the verification contracts' JSON schemas into constrained-decoding grammars within the documented 180-second timeout, because the contracts carry 22-36 optional parameters exceeding Anthropic's effective complexity ceiling.

Story 18ae added a native_structured_output=True row for sonnet-4-6 that wins over the prior _is_claude family rule, routing these models to NativeOutput which sends Bedrock a JSON Schema; this regression was never measured against the largest contracts in the registry.

Every verification finding degrades to no-verification when the verify step fails, leaving reviews unsigned and unclaimable despite blocking=0, because the degrade is deliberate (route through pass3_decide(None)) but the underlying cause is a routing defect, not a verdict defect.

The fix gates NativeOutput on schema complexity (measured bound 16 optional / 12 union, bracketing the observed 14-passes/22-fails gap) and on stack support for outputConfig, falling back to PromptedOutput when either fails, restoring the pre-18ae behavior for only the three measured-failing contracts while preserving 18ae's benefit for small contracts.

Two distinct failure shapes reach the same root cause: Variant A (newer botocore >=1.43.64) hits Bedrock server-side at 180-185s with Grammar compilation timed out; Variant B (main checkout botocore 1.40.61) fails client-side in 0.0s with Unknown parameter outputConfig, both consuming zero tokens and blocking verification entirely.

The fix is load-bearing on recursive optional counting—VerificationOutput has one top-level property with optional fields nested in $defs, so a top-level-only predicate would score contracts at 0-1 and silently reproduce the bug despite appearing to fix it.
